body.statement: Fix \(\gamma\in(c_-,c_+)\), \(q<1/4\), \(r=1\), \(\mu=K=1\), and \(0<\theta<h\) with \(h+\theta/2\le B\). Along \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\), for all sufficiently large \(\ell\) the law \(W_\ell\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(1,1,1,q,B,\theta\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\), satisfies propensity-path stability, and satisfies the primitive oracle gap with \(c_{\mathrm B}=(h-\theta)/\theta\). It has \(b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\asymp\sqrt{\log n_\ell/n_\ell}\). Its marginal row propensity is \(\bar p_i=1/2\), and Markov concentration gives \(\max_i|\widehat p_i-1/2|=O_P(\sqrt{\log n_\ell/m_\ell})\). Consequently \(T^{\mathrm B}=h\mathbf1_{n_\ell}\mathbf1_{m_\ell}^\top+\theta((-1)^{i+j})_{ij}+o_P(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\) in operator norm, so \(\rho_{n_\ell m_\ell}\to2\), \(\widehat\rho_{n_\ell m_\ell}\to2\), \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{n_\ell m_\ell})\), and \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)\to2\). This is a boundary example for \(\mathrm{def:blind\mbox{-}svd}\), not a claim about any published normalization procedure.
body.justification: This explicit calculation is the early kill test and a boundary example for the newly introduced row-fraction procedure.
body.gap: Mehrotra et al.'s public Algorithm 1 also uses empirical row fractions, but it fits the two arm-mean matrices separately under independent assignments; the signed-score procedure in \(\mathrm{def:blind\mbox{-}svd}\) is different, and the predictable Markov witness violates their assignment model. The proposition is therefore a boundary example for the procedure defined here, not a refutation of their theorem or any other published procedure.
body.consumer: HeartSteps-style simulations obtain a fully specified stress design using probabilities \(0.25\) and \(0.75\), with an observed discrepancy that detects failure.
